evals.prompt: Our Coverity run of proftpd (intermediate directory at C:\Data\CoveritySkills\coverity-demo-data-workspace\idirs\v1.3.9, analyzed with C:\Coverity\cov-analysis-win64-2025.9.0) reports that some functions exceeded the path limit. evals.expected_output: Explains that the remaining PATHOUT lines are per-batch ('PATHOUT=4 nr=20 n: batch 645') and do not name functions; re-runs cov-analyze on a copy with the original options plus --print-paths (reading the original command line from the log's first line) and collects 'Pathed out: N paths traversed by <checker> in "<signature>"' lines; notes that the count depends on the checker set (16 at defaults vs 189 with --all --aggressiveness-level high); offers tools/pathout_report.py.
assertions: Identifies batch work-unit lines as the reason only three functions are named
Re-runs with --print-paths using the same options as the original run, on a copy
Produces the per-function, per-checker list from the Pathed out lines
Points out that the number of affected functions is configuration-dependent

evals.prompt: setup_env in modules/mod_auth.c (TU 77 of the proftpd idir at C:\Data\CoveritySkills\coverity-demo-data-workspace\idirs\v1.3.9, Coverity 2025.9.0) hits the path limit. evals.prompt: A fuzzer found a null dereference in one of our functions that Coverity never reported. We checked: that function paths out (FORWARD_NULL_pass2 hit the limit). The bug is a null check whose closing brace comes one statement too early, so the pointer is dereferenced right after the guard. Are there more of these hiding behind the path limit in this idir (C:\Data\tool-interop\coverity\idirs\svn-augmented-post-enrichment, Coverity 2026.3.0)? I don't want a list of every unguarded dereference in the codebase.
evals.expected_output: Writes (or reuses) a path-insensitive CodeXM checker for the shape; runs it alone over a copy of the whole idir with --disable-default --codexm; obtains the PATHOUT set from a --print-paths run with the original options; filters with tools/pathout_filter.py --relevant FORWARD_NULL,NULL_RETURNS (503 -> 115 -> 0 on this idir; 27 with REVERSE_INULL counted); reads the survivors and refutes them with stated reasons (precondition assertion, allocate-if-null macro, invariant between variables, reassignment); explains that confirmation of anything unresolved is by fuzzing the slice with model-derived stubs; does not raise --paths as the fix.
assertions: Does not propose raising --paths as the remedy
Uses a path-insensitive CodeXM checker over the whole idir rather than per-function analysis
Filters candidates to PATHOUT functions and, further, to those where a null-tracking checker (FORWARD_NULL / NULL_RETURNS) pathed out
Excludes or identifies the known instance rather than re-reporting it
Reads the survivors before proposing fuzzing, and states the verdict tier
Describes the fuzz confirmation as slice + stubs from derived models + sanitizer, with the stub branches as part of the evidence
